sections.name: Wanted level one star (police)
sections.card:
Summary: One star is the only level where the police do not use their guns; they try to arrest you instead.
Weak points: The search circle at one star is about two city blocks across, and police cars chase at a moderate speed and try to box you in rather than ram you.
Tips: One star comes from minor things such as attacking civilians, damaging a vehicle, stealing a car in sight of police or passing a toll booth without paying. On foot you can resist arrest, but that jumps you to two stars and the police start shooting; keeping a one-star level for a while also leads to two stars.

sections.name: Wanted level two stars (police shotguns)
sections.card:
Summary: From two stars the police use their guns, which can include pump shotguns, and in chases they try to overtake you or run you off the road.
Danger: More police cars arrive and fit officers in the front passenger seats step out with pump shotguns; if you crash, they use their cars to box you in.
Tips: Two stars come from firing a gun or setting off an explosion near an officer, repeatedly punching an officer, killing many people quickly, destroying a fuel pump at a gas station or a Gruppe 6 Securicar, and resisting arrest.

sections.name: Wanted level three stars (NOOSE, Police Maverick)
sections.card:
Summary: Three stars bring NOOSE, who set up roadblocks on main roads and bridges and send Cruisers and Patriots (the Patriots try to ram you head-on), plus a Police Maverick overhead that shines a spotlight on you at night and fires when its officers get a clear shot.
Weak points: The helicopter now and then breaks off and retreats if you go underground, stay inside a large structure for a long time, or kill both riflemen on board.
Tips: From three stars you can no longer board the subway, and Police Predator patrol boats are sent if you are in or near water. Three stars come from killing or wounding an officer with a gun, or from carrying on with the damage and fighting back at the police.

sections.name: Wanted level four stars (FIB, NOOSE Tactical Response Unit)
sections.card:
Summary: At four stars the FIB or the NOOSE Tactical Response Unit join in, in Enforcer armored vans or FIB Buffalo sedans with four officers each, and the search area grows to about the size of Bohan.
Danger: They carry carbine rifles, some have SMGs and pump shotguns, and they wear body armor, so they take more gunfire before going down.
Tips: They can take around 30 seconds to arrive, and the FIB seems more likely to show up when you drive fast or keep switching vehicles. Four stars also come from entering the runway at Francis International Airport or the grounds of the Civilization Committee in Algonquin.

sections.name: Wanted level five and six stars (Annihilators, snipers)
sections.card:
Summary: At five stars two NOOSE Annihilator helicopters replace the Police Mavericks, and in the main game every officer fires on you while chasing.
Danger: Officers try the PIT maneuver to spin you out, FIB and NOOSE units come in equal numbers, and in areas with tall buildings officers with Combat Sniper rifles shoot at you.
Weak points: An Annihilator is very vulnerable to RPGs and assault rifles, and a single rocket straight into the fuselage destroys it.
Tips: At six stars the search area is about the size of Broker and Dukes, the military is not sent, and officers with PSG-1 sniper rifles keep spawning. Surviving six stars for five minutes earns the One Man Army achievement.

sections.name: Police Maverick
sections.card:
Summary: The police helicopter that arrives at three stars carries a pilot and two riflemen with carbine rifles, and the riflemen shoot you on sight.
Weak points: Its cockpit is exposed, so the people up front can be shot from tall places or with assault rifles, and the lower windows may be a weak spot when it flies above them.
Tips: At four stars NOOSE crew replace the officers aboard if NOOSE is sent, and from five stars an Annihilator can replace the helicopter. Shooting the pilot lets it drift down undamaged about half the time; otherwise it spins and explodes.

sections.name: Yardies
sections.card:
Summary: A loose coalition of Jamaican gangs found mostly around Beechwood City in Broker, with a smaller presence in Schottler and Willis; their cars are painted green, black and gold.
Weapons: They are well armed, with members on the streets carrying pistols, Micro SMGs and pump shotguns.
Tips: Before the mission Shadow they are hostile if you attack them; they welcome you on their turf, and after Shadow they defend you if a pedestrian attacks you.

sections.name: Spanish Lords
sections.card:
Summary: A Puerto Rican street gang, one of the largest in the game, with turf in South Bohan, Fortside (at night only), Cerveza Heights, East Holland and Alderney City, wearing black and gold or red and blue.
Weapons: At night they usually carry Micro SMGs and pistols, and one whose car you hit may step out with a knife.
Tips: In Alderney City they share turf with the Korean Mob and do not fight each other; they sometimes ride in the same car, and both attack you if that car is damaged, and they turn on each other if you start a shoot-out.

sections.name: Body Armor
sections.card:
Summary: A blue vest shown as a blue half-circle bar beside the radar, next to the green health bar; when you aim at an armored target, a small light blue circle shows by the reticle, usually on NOOSE and FIB agents.
Uses: It pads your health against gunfire, explosions and fire, but it gives no protection from falls, being hit by a vehicle on foot, or melee attacks.
Where to get it: The underground gun shops sell it for $500 once the mission Do You Have Protection? is done, it lies about the city with a red glow, and getting into an Enforcer van gives you only about a third of the full amount.

sections.name: Health packs and food
sections.card:
Summary: Health packs shaped like medical kits lie all over Liberty City, mostly in out-of-the-way places, at hospitals and in subway stations.
Uses: Eating at Cluckin' Bell or Burger Shot, or buying from street vendors and vending machines, restores health by different amounts, and drinks usually restore less.
Tips: Dial 911 and then 2 for an ambulance, and the paramedics restore your health for a fee of up to $950, depending on how hurt you are. Maximum health cannot be raised in GTA IV, and saving the game also refills it.

sections.name: Underground Gun Shops
sections.card:
Summary: Three underground gun shops stand in Downtown Broker, Chinatown in Algonquin and Port Tudor in Alderney, and they open with the mission Do You Have Protection?.
Uses: You walk up to a table to look at a gun; ammo costs less than the gun, and the stock grows as the story goes on. A Pistol costs $600, a Pump Shotgun or Micro SMG $1,200, and an Assault Rifle $3,500.
Tips: You cannot enter with a wanted level, because the door stays locked. Do not shoot the clerk: guards loitering at the entrance defend the shop, and if you kill the owner they attack with Combat Shotguns and SMGs and the shop will not sell to you for a while.

sections.name: Car Bomb
sections.card:
Summary: Four blocks of explosive with a phone wired to them, planted under a vehicle and set off by calling Packie and choosing Detonate.
Uses: Setting it off gives you no wanted level, which makes it a handy way to destroy Securicars.
Tips: You get car bombs from Packie as a friend favor, delivered to your general location, and you can place them beneath cars, buses and light vans only.

sections.name: RPG
sections.card:
Summary: The most powerful weapon in the game: a direct hit destroys any target, and the blast hurts everything near it.
Uses: You aim over the shoulder, so you can strafe and shoot from behind cover; the rocket explodes by itself at its maximum range and can be deflected if its tip hits a solid surface at an angle of around 25 degrees.
Tips: The underground gun shops sell it for $15,000 plus $5,000 for each extra rocket once the mission Babysitting is done, and the easiest pickup is on a large boulder in the water north of Northwood. You do not need a direct hit on a helicopter, because the blast can make the pilot lose control and crash.

sections.name: Molotov Cocktail
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown bottle of Cherenkov Vodka that sets things on fire, and the only fire-based weapon you can use.
Uses: One bottle sets an enemy on fire and drops him for a short time, and a second can burn him to death; armored NOOSE and FIB agents may need a third, because body armor suppresses the fire.
Tips: Underground gun shops sell them for $500 after the mission The Master and the Molotov. From a car it is hard to use, as the bottle has to hit the target directly, but four bottles set a car ablaze and six destroy it or leave it unusable.

sections.name: Grenade
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown grenade you can drop at your feet, hold to cook before throwing, or throw back; if you hold it too long it beeps and then explodes in your hand.
Uses: In GTA IV grenades are much more lethal to you than to enemies: unless one blows up very close to an enemy he will likely survive, and enemies run away from a grenade about to explode.
Tips: Dropped from a moving car they beat Molotov Cocktails, because of their far larger blast, but keep driving so your own car is not caught. The underground gun shops sell them for $1,000 after the mission Deconstruction for Beginners.
